record.original_question: For the two Erdős-Freud-Hegyvari sequences defined in the paper—one with a_{2n+2} equal to the smallest missing positive integer and a_{2n+1}=a_{2n}a_{2n+2}, and the other with a_{2n} the smallest unseen positive integer and a_{2n+1}=2a_{2n}—construct the associated 4-regular graphs from their initial segments and explain why these two sequences produce the very interesting graph structures seen empirically. In particular, identify the combinatorial mechanism in the sequences that forces that structure.

evidence.quote: Most of these observations will be purely empirical – thus, we effectively list a large number of open problems: prove that said sequence indeed exhibits the observed type of structure.

The sequences do not seem to have been studied very much: we found them mentioned in a survey article written by Neil Sloane for the Notices [18]. Both sequences result in very interesting graphs (see Fig. 3).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Graph construction. Given a finite sequence a_1, a_2, ..., a_N of pairwise distinct real numbers, build an undirected graph G = (V,E) with vertex set V = {1, 2, ..., N} as follows. For each index i with 2 ≤ i ≤ N, let

  L(i) = argmax { a_j : 1 ≤ j < i and a_j < a_i },
  U(i) = argmin { a_j : 1 ≤ j < i and a_j > a_i }

(when these sets are non‑empty), i.e. L(i) is the index of the largest value strictly less than a_i among the predecessors, and U(i) is the index of the smallest value strictly greater than a_i among the predecessors. Place an edge between i and L(i) and an edge between i and U(i) whenever the corresponding index exists. (Apart from low‑index boundary effects every vertex has degree at most 4, and most vertices have degree exactly 4.)

Two integer sequences. Define two sequences of positive integers (a_n)_{n≥1} as follows.

Sequence S_1 ("multiplicative" Erdős–Freud–Hegyvári rule). Set a_1 = 1, a_2 = 2. For n ≥ 1, let a_{2n+2} be the smallest positive integer that has not yet appeared in the sequence, and set
  a_{2n+1} = a_{2n} · a_{2n+2}.

Sequence S_2 ("doubling" rule). Set a_1 = 1. For n ≥ 1, let a_{2n} be the smallest positive integer that has not yet appeared in the sequence, and set
  a_{2n+1} = 2 · a_{2n}.

Problem. For each of the two sequences S_1 and S_2, build the graph G_N from its initial segment a_1, ..., a_N as described above, and analyse the limiting structure of G_N as N → ∞. Specifically:

(a) Prove that the graphs associated with S_1 and S_2 admit a non-trivial asymptotic geometric/combinatorial structure (for example, a description as a near‑regular planar lattice‑like graph, an explicit decomposition into long paths or cycles, or a bounded‑bandwidth ordering of the vertices).

(b) Identify the combinatorial mechanism within the recursive definitions of S_1 and S_2 — i.e. the interaction between the "smallest missing integer" rule and the multiplicative/doubling rule — that forces this structure, and quantify how the rank of a_n inside the sorted set {a_1, ..., a_n} behaves as n → ∞.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed in a 2020 problem-list preprint stating that the structural observations for these Erdős–Freud–Hegyvári sequences are purely empirical and that proving them constitutes open problems. A web search did not surface any subsequent paper resolving the structure of the graphs associated with these two specific sequences, so the problem appears to remain open.
